root_cause.text: Incorrect wrap detection for 128-byte SQEs in __io_uring_show_fdinfo() uses an increment of sq_head instead of checking the actual array index, leading to failure to detect when a 128-byte SQE’s second half would be past the end of the sq_sqes array, causing an out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "The current check tests (++sq_head & sq_mask) == 0, but sq_head is only incremented when a 128-byte SQE is encountered, not on every iteration. The actual array index is sq_idx = (i + sq_head) & sq_mask, which can be sq_mask (the last slot) while the wrap check passes." The patch changes the condition to `if (sq_idx == sq_mask)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix wrap detection logic for 128-byte SQEs by using sq_idx instead of an incremented counter to correctly identify when an SQE entry would cross the ring boundary.
intent_record.what: Changed the condition for detecting wraparound when processing 128-byte SQEs from 'if ((++sq_head & sq_mask) == 0)' to 'if (sq_idx == sq_mask)' and moved the 'sq_head++' increment to after the if block.
intent_record.how: The old code incremented sq_head before checking for wrap, which could misidentify the boundary. The new code uses sq_idx directly to check if the current index is the last in the ring, and then increments sq_head unconditionally. This ensures the corruption detection correctly identifies when a 128B SQE would cross the ring boundary.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition increments sq_head before checking wrap, but for 128-byte SQEs the correct wrap detection must use the actual array index (sq_idx) to determine if the second half of the SQE would cross the ring boundary. Using the incremented sq_head fails to detect wrap when it should, leading to an out-of-bounds read.
